purpose: Use the receiver declaring owner to load record fields for reads and writes
status: Focused source/metadata and actual archive controls pass; full types gate has one independent active T1693 failure; fresh ordinary post-fix registry replay pending

source_commits.subject: test(types): pin qualified record field assignment owners (T1692)
test(compiler): exercise archived record field owners (T1692)
fix(types): load record fields by resolved nominal owner (T1692)

root_causes: Field reads reduced a resolved qualified nominal owner to its leaf before loading metadata. The fallback could read fields from an unrelated same-name record.
Assignment preflight did not load the full nominal field map. The mounted loader could have owner.__struct_fields_Leaf while the assignment asked for __struct_fields_owner.Leaf.
repair: Reuse the existing transitive metadata loader with the receiver full nominal name for reads and assignment field preflight. No descriptor substitution, new name table, bare-owner fallback or type-specific exception.
causal_boundary: Source imports use parsed ModuleRegistry exports with distinct FileIds; both record owners and source/mount orders are tested.

The compiler fixture uses parsed declarations, compile_core_module_from_ast, archive publication, archive write/read and CoreMetadata bincode write/read before consumer checks. The consumer has empty module ASTs, so source declarations cannot bypass metadata.
Actual archive and metadata body fields are checked independently before every archive consumer matrix. Both scalar types and public visibility remain intact.
Reads, writes and constructor-returned records retain the exact field owner. Wrong field types, sibling-only fields and whole-value owner substitution remain refused.

Full --tests --no-fail-fast execution retains one active missing-module import failure. The repeated builtin snapshot cause is separately tracked as T1693; no new ignore or relaxed assertion was added.
ordinary_boundary: The motivating Response.body diagnostic used the old d61-produced metadata. Root independently confirmed the fresh pre-T1692 stage20 metadata is byte-identical and Response fields remain present. This receipt does not claim a fresh ordinary post-T1692 registry pass, runtime or AOT acceptance.
